declare: `on.request.inputs` is a map of input name to `{type, required, label, help, values, default, min, max}`. Only `type` is required, and any other key is refused when the file is written. `type` is text, textarea, number, bool, date, enum or email (string, integer and select are refused). `values` is the list an enum accepts: required for enum, refused on other types. `min` and `max` bound a number, both inclusive; on other types they are not checked (they do not limit a text's length), and the write gate and `benmore check` warn. A `default` must itself pass the input's checks. An input is read from wherever the request carries its name: path, query string, form or JSON body.
checks: They run before any step, and before a `mode: async` job is queued. text and textarea: a JSON string. number: a JSON number or numeric text (`"2"`, any query or form value). bool: JSON true or false, or the text `true` or `false` (not 1, yes or a checkbox's `on`). date: a real calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD. enum: exactly one of `values`. email: an email address. `required: true` refuses a missing, null or empty-string value. An optional input that is omitted or null takes its `default`, bound like a sent value. Fields the block does not declare are not refused; they bind as usual.
refusal: 422 with `{"error": "flow input \"hours\" is required"}`, naming one input. The other messages end `must be text`, `must be a finite number`, `must be a number within the declared range`, `must be a boolean`, `must be a YYYY-MM-DD date`, `must be one of the declared values` and `must be a valid email address`. With inputs declared, a JSON body that is not one object answers 400 `{"error": "Flow request body must be a JSON object"}`.
clients: bm.flows.<name>(params, body) gets a typed body: number is `number`, bool `boolean`, enum the union of its values, the others `string`, and required inputs are required fields. A GET flow's inputs are fields of its one params argument and travel in the query string. FlowForm (api({at:'components'})) renders one control per input, sorted by name: `label` (else the name), a select for enum, a checkbox for bool, min and max on a number field, `default` as the starting value, `required`. `help` and every other field reach your own UI through GET /_internal/flows.json; FlowForm does not show `help`.
yaml_example:
# flows/log-time.yaml - POST /api/tasks/:id/time with a typed, validated body
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/tasks/:id/time
    auth: required
    inputs:
      hours:     { type: number, required: true, min: 0.25, max: 24, label: "Hours" }
      kind:      { type: enum, values: [dev, review, meeting], default: dev }
      billable:  { type: bool, default: true }
      worked_on: { type: date }
      note:      { type: textarea, help: "Shown on the invoice" }
jobs:
  log:
    steps:
      - id: task
        run: sql
        with: { query: "SELECT id FROM tasks WHERE id = :id AND user_id = :user_id" }
      - if: ${{ !steps.task.outputs.rows }}
        run: respond
        with: { status: 404, json: { error: task_not_found } }
      - id: entry
        run: sql
        with:
          query: "INSERT INTO time_entries (task_id, hours, kind, billable, worked_on, note, user_id) VALUES (:id, :hours, :kind, :billable, :worked_on, :note, :user_id) RETURNING id"
          params:
            billable: "${{ params.billable }}"            # a whole-value boolean binds 1/0
            worked_on: "${{ params.worked_on || '' }}"    # optional inputs need a fallback
            note: "${{ params.note || '' }}"
      - run: respond
        with:
          status: 201
          json: { id: "${{ steps.entry.outputs.id }}", kind: "${{ params.kind }}", hours: "${{ params.hours }}" }
